blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Structuring a complex cross-border deal is the nearest thing in trade to three-dimensional chess. You are holding, in mind, a product or commodity, a buyer in one jurisdiction, a seller in another, a financier in a third, perhaps an intermediary in a fourth, and a transport and insurance chain running through two or three more. Every decision in one corner ripples across the others.

The art is to work from the risks outward. Start with the full list of risks — default, delay, quality dispute, regulatory change, FX, customs. For each, identify which party is best placed to carry, insure, or hedge it. Then design the contractual and financial architecture that puts each risk exactly where the analysis says it should be. The result is often a structure the two sides would never have reached by arguing point by point.

The language of this work is dense, populated with phrases like under the terms of, with reference to, in consideration of, and subject to the approval of. Learning it well is less about memorising phrases and more about learning to think in their shape.

items.q: According to the text, what is the recommended starting point when structuring a deal?
items.why: "Start with the full list of risks… work from the risks outward."

items.q: Once the risks are listed, what should be decided for each one?
options: Which clause to cite in the contract
Which party is best placed to carry, insure, or hedge it
How much the deal will cost in total
Which jurisdiction has the friendliest courts
items.why: "identify which party is best placed to carry, insure, or hedge it."

items.q: The comparison to "three-dimensional chess" is meant to convey that the work is…
options: a competitive game with a single winner
highly interdependent, where each move affects many others
governed by fixed and predictable rules
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora reforça que "every decision in one corner ripples across the others".

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A good structure allocates each risk to the right party.
The best deals are reached by arguing clause by clause until one side concedes.
The specialised language exists because precision matters.
Cross-border deals involve several interacting jurisdictions.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a boa estrutura é a que "the two sides would never have reached by arguing point by point".

items.q: What does the closing line — "learning to think in their shape" — suggest about the dense legal language?
options: It is decorative and can safely be ignored
Mastery comes from internalising its logic, not just rote-learning phrases
It should be simplified before use in real deals
Only lawyers ever need to understand it
items.why: Inferência: "less about memorising phrases and more about learning to think in their shape" — trata-se de absorver a lógica.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conduzindo a estruturação do negócio entre as cinco partes. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me walk everyone through where we've landed, because this is a five-party structure and the pieces only make sense together.

We started, as always, from the risks rather than the clauses. The biggest one is quality dispute on arrival in Asia — so we've placed inspection at the port of loading in Brazil, with the certificate released only on the buyer's nominated surveyor signing off. That means the seller carries the goods until inspection, and the risk transfers cleanly at that point, not before.

The financier in Europe is nervous about FX exposure over the ninety-day term, which is fair. So the facility is drawn in dollars, and we've hedged the real leg separately, in consideration of a slightly higher margin. The two insurers split the chain: one covers marine transit, the other covers political and regulatory change, subject to the approval of their reinsurers, which we should hear on by Friday.

Now, the intermediary. I know some of you would rather cut them out. But under the terms we've drafted, they absorb the customs and delay risk on the Asian side — a risk none of the other four wanted. Remove them, and that risk lands back on us. So my recommendation is that we keep the structure as it stands.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Emily say the team began building the structure?
options: From the list of risks rather than the clauses
items.why: "We started, as always, from the risks rather than the clauses."

items.q: How is the quality-dispute risk handled in the structure?
options: Inspection happens at the port of loading, with the certificate released on the surveyor signing off
The buyer inspects the goods only after they arrive in Asia
The seller waives all responsibility for quality
The insurers cover any quality dispute directly
items.why: "we've placed inspection at the port of loading in Brazil, with the certificate released only on the buyer's nominated surveyor signing off."

items.q: Why is the facility drawn in dollars with the real leg hedged separately?
options: To reduce the financier's FX exposure over the ninety-day term
Because the buyer insisted on dollar payment
Because Brazilian banks would not lend
items.why: "The financier… is nervous about FX exposure over the ninety-day term… So the facility is drawn in dollars, and we've hedged the real leg separately."

items.q: What does Emily imply would happen if the intermediary were removed?
options: The customs and delay risk would fall back on their own side
The insurers would lower their premiums
The financier would increase the facility
items.why: Inferência: "they absorb the customs and delay risk… Remove them, and that risk lands back on us."

items.q: What is Emily's overall stance on the current structure?
options: She wants to renegotiate it from scratch
She is defending it as a deliberate allocation of risk and recommends keeping it
She is indifferent to whether it changes
She thinks the intermediary should be cut out
items.why: Inferência: ela justifica cada peça pelo risco que carrega e conclui "my recommendation is that we keep the structure as it stands".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A single tariff change in one market can ripple through the entire structure." Here, ripple means to…
options: spread its effects outward across the other parts
items.why: Ripple = repercutir, propagar efeitos de um ponto para os demais.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ sits between producer and buyer, absorbing the customs and delay risk that neither side wanted."
items.why: Intermediary = intermediário, a parte que se interpõe entre produtor e comprador.

items.q: "The contractual architecture is the skeleton of the deal." This phrase refers to…
options: the physical office where the deal is signed
the overall design of how the contracts fit together
the legal fees charged by counsel
items.why: Contractual architecture = arquitetura contratual: o desenho de como os contratos se encaixam.

items.q: "The facility is subject to the approval of the reinsurers." This means the facility is…
options: conditional on their approval being given
items.why: Subject to = sujeito a: depende dessa condição para valer.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "The extra margin was granted ___ the additional hedging the financier had to arrange."
items.why: In consideration of = em consideração a / em contrapartida por: a margem é a contrapartida do hedge extra.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na estruturação de negócios internacionais. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The reinsurers still have to sign off on the political-risk cover." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the structure shipment by shipment once the first cargo clears." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, etapa por etapa.

items.q: "The buyer pushed back on the inspection point, wanting it moved to the port of discharge." They…
options: resisted it and argued for a different arrangement
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — propor alternativa sem necessariamente rejeitar tudo.

items.q: "Everyone agreed the hedging plan, but nobody followed through on booking the forward." They…
options: failed to carry it through to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, ninguém o fez.

items.q: "Shaving a few basis points off the margin won't move the needle on the buyer's overall cost." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
